Built by mechanical carry-forward from pricing-2026-09-07.json: a script asserted zero drift on all 17 carried rows (base input/output, 5m and 1h cache writes, cache hits, fast mode) against the live table before any delta was applied. THE LOAD-BEARING CHANGE: Opus 5.5 prices cache hits at 0.05x base input ($0.20/MTok on $4) — pricing page footnote 2 — so cache-read pricing now has three multipliers: 0.1x default, 0.05x Opus 5.5, 0.025x Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1. RESOLUTION ORDER for the cache-read multiplier: the model entry's own `cache.read_multiplier` first, then this sheet's global `cache.read_multiplier`. Opus 5.5 has been Claude Code's DEFAULT model on every paid plan since v2.1.280 (2026-09-22), so `claude-opus-5-5` rows are landing in local data now; in the 2026-09-07 sheet they fell to the opus family fallback and were priced at Opus 5's rates (2.5x on every cache read). Opus 5 stays priced and Active. Rates here are per million tokens, standard first-party Claude API. Partner-operated platforms (Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud) publish their own pricing and are NOT covered by this sheet. Also corrected 2026-09-27 from primaries read that day: mythos-5-1 now has a deprecations row (Active, not sooner than 2027-09-01); max_20x's $200 is now VERIFIED (Help Center 11049741, slugged URL); the Fable 5 promotional credits EXPIRED 2026-09-17 at 11:59 PM PT. opus-5-5.note: Claude Code's DEFAULT model on every paid plan since v2.1.280 (2026-09-22) — Pro and Team Standard moved from Sonnet to Opus that day, and the default Opus became Opus 5.5 — so `claude-opus-5-5` rows arrive in local data without the user choosing them. In the 2026-09-07 sheet this id missed every key and fell to the opus family fallback (Opus 5's rates, flagged unpriceable). Cache hits and refreshes are 0.05x base input ($0.20/MTok), NOT the global 0.1x: pricing page footnote 2, 'Cache hits and refreshes on Claude Opus 5.5 are priced at 0.05x the base input price.' Cache writes use the global multipliers ($5 5-minute, $8 1-hour = 1.25x / 2x of $4). Fast mode $8/$40; 'Prompt caching multipliers apply on top of fast mode pricing', so a fast cache read is 0.05 x $8 = $0.40/MTok — DERIVED by that stated rule, not printed on the page. Batch $2/$10 (API-only; never in Claude Code data). 1M context at standard rates, 128K max output, adaptive thinking always on, default effort `medium` (Opus 5's is `high`), reliable knowledge cutoff Jun 2026. Cache minimum 512 tokens (prompt-caching docs, read 2026-09-27). Anthropic's own claim that it 'costs 40% less to run than Opus 5' is THEIR measurement from THEIR tests, partly fewer tokens per task; what the rates alone say is that identical tokens cost 20% less in and out and cache reads 60% less. compare-models re-prices recorded tokens at fixed counts, so it shows the rate difference only.

opus-5.note: Claude Code's default `opus` from v2.1.219 until v2.1.280 (2026-09-22), when Opus 5.5 replaced it as the default Opus. Still ACTIVE on the Claude API, retirement not sooner than 2027-07-24 (model-deprecations status table, read 2026-09-27). claude.com/pricing now labels it 'Opus 5 (Legacy)'; that is marketing framing, NOT lifecycle state, and nothing we publish may call Opus 5 deprecated or retired. Dropped from the `compare-models` comparison set on 2026-09-27 in favour of opus-5-5, but fully priced here so historical turns still cost correctly. Thinking is ON by default (effort `high`); `thinking: disabled` returns 400 at xhigh/max effort. 1M context at standard rates. Cache minimum is 512 tokens — small cache lines on this model are normal, not anomalies. Cache hits are the global 0.1x ($0.50/MTok) — Opus 5 did NOT get Opus 5.5's 0.05x.

fable-5-1.note: Claude Code's DEFAULT Fable model since v2.1.257 (2026-09-01) — not an opt-in, so these rows arrive in local data without the user choosing them. Cache hits and refreshes are 0.025x base input ($0.25/MTok), NOT the global 0.1x: see this entry's `cache` block and the sheet note. Same $10/$50 base as Fable 5, so the ONLY price difference between the two is the cache-read multiplier — 4x. 1M context, 128K max output, thinking adaptive and always on, API default effort `high`, reliable knowledge cutoff Jun 2026. Billing depends on the user's plan, not on a date — see the `fable` block, which is family-scoped and which Fable 5.1 inherits.

fable-5.note: Requires Claude Code 2.1.170 or later. Thinking cannot be disabled on Fable 5. Cache hits are the global 0.1x ($1/MTok) — Fable 5 did NOT get the 0.025x multiplier that fable-5-1 and mythos-5-1 carry, even though the base rates are identical. STILL ACTIVE on the Claude API, retirement not sooner than 2027-06-09 (model-deprecations status table, re-read 2026-09-27). claude.com/pricing and the models-overview page both file it under a 'Legacy models' heading; that is marketing/grouping framing, NOT lifecycle state, and nothing we publish may call Fable 5 deprecated, retired or unsupported. Dropped from the `compare-models` comparison set on 2026-09-07 in favour of fable-5-1, but fully priced here so historical turns still cost correctly. Billing depends on the user's plan, not on a date — see the `fable` block.

mythos-5-1.note: On the public pricing table at limited availability, but not selectable in Claude Code, so it should never appear in local Claude Code data. Priced here so that if it ever does appear it costs correctly instead of resolving to null — the same treatment mythos-5 gets. Carries the same 0.025x cache-read multiplier as fable-5-1 (pricing page footnote 1). CORRECTED 2026-09-27: the model-deprecations status table now carries a row for `claude-mythos-5-1` — Active, retirement not sooner than 2027-09-01. The 2026-09-07 sheet recorded no date because the table had no row then; that note ('limited-availability models are not listed') is no longer true.

mythos-5.note: On the public pricing table at limited availability, but not selectable in Claude Code, so it should never appear in local Claude Code data. Priced here so that if it ever does appear it costs correctly instead of resolving to null. Cache hits are the global 0.1x ($1/MTok): the 0.025x footnote names Mythos 5.1, not Mythos 5. Retirement not sooner than 2027-06-09 (model-deprecations status table, read 2026-09-27).

family_fallback.note: Last resort only. When it fires it resolves to the NEWEST opus key by sort order, never to whichever key happens to come first in the object, and the caller is handed fallback: true, priceable: false. HARDENED 2026-09-27: that flag is NOT enough on its own. When Opus 5.5 shipped (2026-09-22) this fallback priced `claude-opus-5-5` at Opus 5's rates — cache reads at $0.50 against a true $0.20 — and every surface that read the rate without checking `fallback` presented the guess as ours (`wtclaude waste` did; the browser mirror carried no flag at all). The rule now: a family-fallback rate never produces a figure presented as ours. Consumers either exclude the turn and say so (compare-models, whatif) or withhold the figure (waste). There is deliberately NO fable family fallback, and none may be added: Fable 5 and Fable 5.1 carry different cache-read multipliers on identical base rates. The same is now true of Opus (Opus 5 0.1x, Opus 5.5 0.05x), which is exactly why the opus fallback is flagged rather than trusted.

cache.note: THREE cache-read multipliers as of 2026-09-27 (pricing page §Prompt caching, verbatim: 'Cache read (hit): 0.1x base input price (0.025x on Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1; 0.05x on Claude Opus 5.5)'). `read_multiplier` here is the DEFAULT 0.1x; a model entry's own `cache.read_multiplier` wins when present. Resolution order: model override -> this global default. Overrides: fable-5-1 and mythos-5-1 at 0.025x ($0.25/MTok on $10), opus-5-5 at 0.05x ($0.20/MTok on $4). Every other row inherits 0.1x, which is correct for all of them. Do NOT collapse this back to a single global number: Fable 5 and Fable 5.1 share a $10 base input and differ ONLY in cache reads ($1 vs $0.25), and Opus 5 vs Opus 5.5 cache reads differ 2.5x ($0.50 vs $0.20). A model missing its override is silently wrong — nothing throws. Cache WRITE multipliers remain global — the live table shows 1.25x (5m) and 2x (1h) of base input for every row, including Opus 5.5 ($5 / $8 on $4) and the 5.1s, with no per-model exception. Caching multipliers also apply ON TOP of fast mode pricing (pricing page §Fast mode). CARRIED FORWARD 2026-08-24: the write multipliers were corrected then from 0.25, which under-priced every cache write 5-8x. `write_multiplier` is the effective default used when the payload cannot tell us the TTL, and it is set to the 1-hour rate because that is what Claude Code subscription sessions actually bill: the costs doc states subscription cache lifetime is 1 hour, and fitting 24 clean local sessions against their billing-grade cost anchors implies a multiplier of 2.10 (median), reconstructing 0.991 of the anchor at 2.0x versus 0.899 at 1.25x. On credits-billed usage the cache lifetime collapses to 5 minutes unless ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1 is set (default off), which moves the correct multiplier to 1.25x. We cannot see that crossing in local data, so this is a labeled default, not a measurement of any individual turn.

modifiers.note: Documented so no surface maintains its own copy of these numbers. NONE of them are applied to the headline figure: the headline is the payload's own cost.total_cost_usd, which already has every applicable modifier baked in. Re-applying the 1.1x residency multiplier on top of the anchor would double-count. Batch (-50% both directions) is an API-surface concept and never appears in Claude Code data. Claude 4.6 and later include the full 1M context window at standard rates, so long context carries no premium; models before 4.6 return 400 on the inference_geo parameter.

fable.promo_credit_expiry_note: 11:59 PM PT, regardless of when the credit was claimed. EXPIRED — 2026-09-17 has passed. `promo_credit_expires_at` is that instant in Pacific Daylight Time (UTC-7 in September). Re-read 2026-09-27 by the PMO: Help Center 15862783 (title 'Claude Fable 5 one-time free credits promotion') still states 'The promotional credit expires on September 17, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT'. First VERIFIED 2026-09-07: 'These new promotional credits expire on September 17, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT, 60 days after the promotion begins' and 'you can claim your promotional credits through August 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT'. While live, promo credits were spent before other credits, including auto-reload, silently. SCOPE: these credits were FABLE 5 ONLY. Help Center 15424964: the one-time credit 'applied to the Fable 5 change only, and there's no equivalent credit for Fable 5.1.' Eligibility was Pro and Team standard seats held as of 2026-07-19. fable.note: FAMILY-SCOPED, not model-scoped (reworded 2026-09-07). Fable became a PERMANENT, PLAN-CONDITIONAL offering on 2026-07-20 — it is not a date cliff any more. The mechanic attaches to Fable as a family, not to any one Fable model: claude.com/pricing states the plan rows generically as 'Fable', so Claude Fable 5.1 inherits exactly the same mechanic Fable 5 has, and any future Fable inherits it too. On Max, Team Premium and Enterprise Premium, Fable is included up to 50 percent of the weekly usage limit; that is a share OF the weekly limit, not an allowance on top of it, and it is not a credits wallet. On Pro and Team Standard, Fable bills usage credits from the first token. historical_boundary_date is retained only so records from before 2026-07-20 can be interpreted under the old mechanic; it is NOT a future event and must never be rendered as a countdown.
fable.historical_boundary_note: 2026-07-19 is when the PREVIOUS mechanic ended — the promotion that let Pro and Team-standard users spend up to 50% of the weekly subscription limit on Fable 5 at no extra cost. Help Center 15424964, read 2026-09-07: 'That promotion ended on July 19, 2026 at 11:59:59 PM PT, and it applied to Fable 5 only. Claude Fable 5.1 was never part of it.' Do not confuse this date with promo_credit_expiry — they are different mechanics that happen to sit two months apart.
fable.plan_rows_note: B2, settled 2026-09-07. claude.com/pricing's 'Models and usage' table collapses Team into a SINGLE column reading 'No' for Fable. That is a page simplification, NOT a change in Team Fable access: the same page's plan card still sells two Team seat types (Standard $20/$25, Premium $100/$125), and Help Center 15424964 states the split explicitly — Fable is included on 'Max plans, premium seats on Team plans, and premium seats on legacy seat-based Enterprise plans', while on 'Pro plans, Team standard seats and Enterprise standard seats' it runs on usage credits. included_plans and credits_plans below are therefore CORRECT as encoded and were deliberately left unchanged. The same article states 'Fable 5 and Fable 5.1 work the same way on your plan', which is the primary-sourced basis for this block being family-scoped.

credits.note: Usage credits DO expire. In effect since 2026-09-10. VERIFIED 2026-09-07 and re-read by the PMO 2026-09-27 (slugged URL https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12429409-manage-usage-credits-for-paid-claude-plans, wording unchanged): 'In most cases, usage credits do not expire. However, in certain jurisdictions such as Japan, usage credits expire six months after purchase starting September 10, 2026.' A 7-day email warning is sent and expiry dates are visible on the Usage page. The exact jurisdiction set is not published — Japan is given as an example, not as the complete list — so 'credits don't expire' is not a safe sentence anywhere. Separately, pre-purchased usage bundles discount the effective rate by up to 30 percent ($50 to $45, $250 to $200, $1000 to $700), and local data cannot see which bundle a user holds — so every credits-denominated figure we print is at standard list rates and must say so.
